newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tankan confirms gradual Japan economy recovery - BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Tankan confirms gradual Japan economy recovery - BOJ.

text.p: The results of the Bank of Japan's "tankan" corporate survey, unveiled earlier on Wednesday, confirms Japan's economy is gradually recovering, Masayuki Matsushima, director of the Bank of Japan's Research and Statistics Department, told a news conference.
"Looking at the overall picture, the results (of the tankan) back up our view that the economy is gradually recovering," Matsushima said.
Asked whether the results of the tankan would improve the central bank's assessment of the economy, Matsushima said: "The situation is not of the sort that would make us change our assessment."
Asked whether the pace of Japan's recovery has slowed somewhat, he said: "Although the recovery is not without setbacks, the doors to recovery have not been shut. The recovery is still continuing."
In its August tankan survey announced earlier in the day, the BOJ said the diffusion index for major manufacturers fell to minus seven from minus three in the previous May survey.
Matsushima attributed the drop in the index mainly to delays in inventory adjustments in the paper/pulp and steel industries.
However, he said prospects were brighter because stock adjustments were being carried out steadily and domestic demand was on a recovery trend.

The diffusion index for major non-manufacturing companies showed an improvement, helped by better business conditions in the service and leasing industries, he said. Business sentiment among small and medium-sized companies was only slightly better, affected by adjustments in production by bigger firms.
The tankan showed an upward revision in companies' capital investment plans.
"This result is in line with our assessment that an improvement in capital spending is spreading to all industries and to companies of various sizes," Matsushima said.
However, the worsening condition of the microchip market was not adequately reflected in the August tankan, he said.
Due to the slowness in the microchip market "there is still a possibility that companies may consider cutting down their capital spending," Matsushima said.

Also, the yen's recent weakness had not been fully incorporated into the results of the August tankan, so the central bank would like to keep careful watch over changes in companies' business plans in the coming months, Matsushima said.
Asked if the BOJ was certain Japan's economic recovery would continue for the time being, he said the central bank would monitor future economic indicators to determine whether it would continue.
The results of the tankan alone would not change the BOJ's views on the overall economic trend, Matsushima added.
